Purpose of processing: To guarantee high quality and safety standards of our medical devices, i.e., the Ada Health App and Ada Assess, it is necessary to systematically monitor their quality, performance and safety (“Post-Market-Surveillance”).
Purpose of processing: We process some usage data (which does not include personal health data) if you are using the App, to understand how Ada reaches people online.
Purpose of processing: Ada implements a variety of technical and organisational measures to ensure that your data is adequately protected.
Purpose of processing: We process you data to send you direct marketing (products and services) or communication about any survey that we believe will be of interest to you.
Purpose of processing: We use a limited set of usage data (which does not include personal health data) to track your page interaction and analyze the data to optimize our marketing initiatives.

Purpose of processing: We use the above data (which does not include personal health data) to ensure the proper use, functioning, maintenance and improvement of our Services (our Services cannot function properly without this processing) as well as to prevent any decompiling or otherwise reverse engineering.
Purpose of processing: Ada is relying on feedback and surveys in various scenarios to understand if and how our products can be improved to match your needs.
Purpose of processing: Based on your consent, we can contact you via push notifications in the Ada app to help you make the best use of Ada’s functionalities.

Purpose of processing: We will use data that we have stored about you to the extent that this is necessary to exercise a legal claim of our own or to defend us against a legal claim you file against us.

Purpose of processing: Ada will share your data with a government entities such as a law enforcement agencies to the extent that it is necessary to prevent harm to others and to yourself or required by applicable law or required to comply with a valid court order, subpoena, search warrant or other order by a competent authority.

If your personal data is used for more than one purpose, we will retain it until the purpose with the longest period expires, but we will stop using it for the purpose with the shorter period as soon as the shorter period expires (to comply with the purpose limitation principle).

justification: The policy explicitly specifies purposes for each data processing activity in section 3, ensuring they are determined at collection as required by Article 5(1)(b) and Recital 39. Each purpose is legitimate, such as providing services or complying with legal obligations, and data use is limited to those stated purposes without repurposing. This structure links data types directly to explicit purposes, preventing undefined or illegitimate use.

article_5_text: Adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary … ("data minimization").

justification: The policy lists specific, relevant data types for each purpose in section 3, ensuring collection is limited to what is necessary as per Article 5(1)(c) and Recital 39. It emphasizes optional data and warns that without certain information, functionalities may be limited, avoiding unnecessary collection. article_5_text: Accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date … ("accuracy").
recital_39_reference: Every reasonable step should be taken to ensure that personal data which are inaccurate are rectified or deleted.

policy_clauses.quote: When you update information such as height and weight in your profile, we will keep the previous entries to allow you to track its development.
In some cases, the accuracy of the results might be impacted.

Right to Rectification: As a data subject, you have the right to rectification under the conditions provided in Article 16 GDPR. This means in particular that you have the right to receive from us, without undue delay, the rectification of inaccuracies in your personal data and completion of incomplete personal data.

Such a review can be prompted by your medically relevant feedbackor a lodged complaint. If you voluntarily share findings of your medical treatment we will use this information for purposes of Post-Market-Surveillance as well.

justification: The policy allows users to update profiles and provides a right to rectification under Article 16 GDPR, aligning with the accuracy requirement in Article 5(1)(d) by enabling correction of inaccuracies. However, it lacks explicit mention of proactive steps by the controller to verify or update data where necessary, such as periodic reviews, relying instead on user-initiated changes and feedback. This partially meets Recital 39's call for reasonable steps to rectify or delete inaccurate data, but could be stronger with internal accuracy measures.

article_5_text: Kept in a form which permits identification … no longer than is necessary … ("storage limitation").

justification: The policy defines specific, minimal storage durations tied to purposes in section 3 and 7, ensuring data is not kept identifiable longer than necessary per Article 5(1)(e) and Recital 39. policy_clauses.quote: For Ada Health GmbH (“Ada”, “us”, “our” or “we”) it is vitally important that our customers (the “users”) feel secure when using our products and services.

We use the above data to provide you with access to our Services, to ensure that the Services can establish an internet connection smoothly and are easy to use. We also use this data to analyze the system security and stability, as well as for additional administrative purposes.
We have entered into a Data Protection Agreement with Cloudflare. Cloudflare is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework ensuring and adequate level of data protection.
No data will be shared with any third party without your specific consent.
Your data is only processed internally at Ada and will not be shared with our partners.

We use the ‘Braze’ service provided by Braze Inc., 330 W 34th St 18th floor, New York, NY 10001, USA as our technical service provider in the USA to deliver the relevant emails. Braze is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, which ensures an adequate level of data protection.
Before we share any data with Tableau, we remove all information that directly identifies you.

To the extent possible, we use pseudonymized or anonymized data and to perform this task. However, in some circumstances your (sensitive) personal information might also be processed in the clear, e.g., where it is necessary to reach out to you.
We will never share your personal health information with advertisers or other third parties for this purpose.

Ada implements a variety of technical and organisational measures to ensure that your data is adequately protected. The implementation of these measures is expressly required by law in Art. 32 GDPR and is also needed for the ISO 27001 certification of Ada's information security management system. The implementation of these security measures may require the processing of your data, for example, to verify your email address or to create and maintain backups. Ada also runs bug bounty programs in which we hire external security experts to scan our systems for vulnerabilities. Further information on these programs can be found here. The processing of your personal data is not intended for the purposes of these programs, but it cannot be completely ruled out either. For this unlikely event, we conclude a data processing agreement with all third parties involved in accordance with Art. 28 GDPR.

We use the ‘Braze’ service provided by Braze Inc., 330 W 34th St 18th floor, New York, NY 10001, USA as our technical service provider in the USA to deliver the relevant emails. Braze is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, which ensures an adequate level of data protection.

We only use pseudonymized usage data that we may collect via service of our processor Functional Software Inc., 132 Hawthorne Street, San Francisco, California 94107 USA (“Sentry”). This data may be transmitted to and stored on Sentry’s servers. For more information, please see Sentry’s privacy policy here. We may also send the above personal data to our processor Sumo Logic, a corporation headquartered at 305 Main Street, Redwood City, CA 94063, US. The data collected in the context is not used to link any usage profile with your personal data. Your personal data may be transmitted and stored into the servers of Sumo Logic. Further information can be found in Sumo Logic’s Privacy Statement here. We also transfer the personal data to our processor Hound Technology, Inc., 548 Market Street, 25362 San Francisco, CA 94104-5401 (“Honeycomb”). The data processed in this context is pseudonymized and cannot be linked to you by Honeycomb. Ada does not link any usage profile with your personal data. Further information can be found in Honeycomb’s Privacy Policy here. All service providers are certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework ensuring and adequate level of data protection.

To deliver the push notifications we use the Service “Braze” of the Braze Inc., 330 W 34th St 18th floor, New York, NY 10001, USA as our technical service provider which processes your data in the US. Braze only has access to a limit data set in order to be able to technically deliver the push notification to your device. It does not have access to your health or app usage data. We have entered into a Data Processing Agreement with Braze whereby Braze is solely allowed to process your data according to Ada’s instructions. Braze is certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework ensuring and adequate level of data protection.

When you delete your account, we need to ensure that the information is still available to us for a period of time in which litigation over Ada’s services appears likely. For that time, we will encrypt and vault your data including your health information to have it accessible in the event of a subsequent lawsuit. Your data can only be accessed by limited personal subject to a procedure that involves approval by our Data Processing Officer. Your data will not be used for any other purpose during that time.

The personal data that we collect from you is stored in the European Union on Cloud Servers of Amazon Web Services EMEA S.A.R.L. (“AWS”) with a business seat in Luxembourg and on the Cloud Servers of Google Commerce Limited ("GCL"), a company incorporated under the laws of Ireland, with its offices at Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland.

Sensitive information between your browser and our Website is transferred in encrypted form using Transport Layer Security (“TLS”). When transmitting sensitive information, you should always make sure that your browser can validate our certificate.

Ada shares your personal data with third parties to provide you with its services or as required in the course of its business. Ada does not share your data for third-party commercial interests without your explicit consent.
We use technical service providers to operate and maintain our Services, who act as our processors based on data processing agreements as required by Art. 28 GDPR.

Where we use Service providers who process personal data on our behalf outside the EEA (or “third countries”) we do so with the appropriate safeguards for your data subject rights. Most of our US service providers are certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Where this is not the case, we have agreed on the Standard Contractual Clauses with added securities (where necessary).
We restrict access to your personal data to the persons who need to use it for the relevant purpose(s), always in compliance with the integrity and confidentiality principle.

After the processing of your data is no longer necessary for the purposes outlined in section 3 or your account is deleted (see section 3.2) we will securely and separately store some of your data in accordance with statutory retention obligations applicable to us and reasonable business needs.
If the processing of your personal data is no longer necessary for any purpose it is either irreversibly anonymized (and the anonymized data may be retained), or securely erased.

justification: The policy details technical and organizational measures like encryption, pseudonymization, and access restrictions to ensure security, meeting Article 5(1)(f)'s requirement for appropriate protection against unauthorized processing or loss. It uses DPAs, EU-US Data Privacy Framework certifications, and Standard Contractual Clauses for international transfers, demonstrating integrity and confidentiality. While Recital 39 focuses more on lawfulness and transparency, the policy's clear descriptions of these measures support fair and transparent security practices.

article_5_text: The controller shall be responsible for, and be able to demonstrate compliance … ("accountability").
recital_39_reference: Recital 39 does not address accountability (focuses on Art. 5(1)(a)-(f)). Recital 39 silent on Art. 5(2); evaluate it based on article 5(2).
